newsitem.title: USA: SEC opposes toughening burden in shareholder suits.
newsitem.headline: SEC opposes toughening burden in shareholder suits.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission Tuesday joined the fray in a lawsuit against Silicon Graphics Inc. by a group of shareholders, urging a court not to make such cases more difficult to win.
In a friend of the court brief, the SEC asked a U.S. District Court in San Francisco to reconsider a key deterimination it reached when it dismissed the shareholders' original complaint.

The court ruled that under the 1995 Private Securities Litigation Reform Act, shareholders who claimed that they lost money because of false and misleading information issued by a company must allege that there was "conscious behaviour" by the company and must infer strongly that the company made "knowing" misrepresentations.

Those standards would be more difficult for shareholder plaintiffs to prove than claiming that misrepresentations were the result merely of "reckless behaviour" by the companies, which had been sufficient grounds for plaintiffs to prevail.

SEC General Counsel Richard Walker said the agency did not believe the 1995 act weakened the so-called recklessness standard, which he said is needed to protect investors and markets that rely upon company disclosures.
"While Congress certainly sought to strengthen the pleading requirements in private securities fraud actions, it clearly did not intend to eliminate liability for reckless behaviour," said Walker.

Walker said the Silicon Graphics case was the only one of three or four cases litigated since enactment of the act in which a federal court determined that recklessness was not sufficient for a plaintiff to allege fraud against a company.
In filing its brief, he stressed that the SEC was not taking sides in the dispute between the company and the shareholders.
"We don't express any views on the merits of the lawsuits," he said.

The case against Mountain View, Calif.-based Silicon Graphics, filed by San Diego attorney William Lerach, is a class action suit in which the company is alleged to have artificially inflated the price of its stock through false and misleading statements.
